newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close weaker on inflation, property sector fears.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close weaker on inflation, property sector fears.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Thursday for the first time in four days, as U.S. inflation and local property market fears eroded sentiment, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index was down 67.98 points or 0.55 percent at 12,358.7. Turnover was HK$8.18 billion, significantly higher than Wednedsay's HK$6.66 billion.

"Basically, (it's) East Point -- 52 units only taken up out of 215," said James Osborn, sales director at Barings, referring to a sale of flats in the New Territories by blue chip property company Sung Hung Kai Properties Ltd.

Osborn said the sale had compounded bearish comments on the property sector by Lee Shau-kee, chairman of Henderson Land Development Co Ltd that secondary market flat prices had dropped between five percent and 10 percent since early March.
The property sector jitters, combined with overnight losses on Wall Street, took the heart out of local investors, at one time pushing the Hang Seng Index down more than 100 points.
"I think they're (Wall Street and the property market) both combining to create a poor sentiment at this time," said Grant Forster, vice president, BT Fund Managers.
Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel's institutional sales said the sale of a new Henderson development would "roughly confirm" whether Hong Kong's property prices were dipping.
Investors were still looking at China plays, red chips, and even H shares like Maanshan Iron and Steel Co Ltd, said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager with Nikko Securities.
Shares in red chip Shanghai Industrial closed up HK$0.30 at HK$35.80 after a placement of 139.47 million new shares.
China Light shares surged HK$1.00 to HK$34.50 on the news that it had signed a joint venture agreement with Exxon Energy Ltd, a subsidiary of Exxon Corp, to build a plant in China.
China Light's 20 percent shareholder, red chip CITIC Pacific Ltd, fell HK$0.20 to HK$37.70.

In the property sector Sun Hung Kai led the losses, falling $1.00 to HK$76.50, New World Development lost HK$0.98 to HK$40.30, and Sino Land which plans a convertible bond issue, fell HK$0.20 to HK$7.40.
Among the banks, HSBC lost HK$0.50 to HK$181, while Dah Sing lost HK$0.88 to HK$31.00.
